hints: Look for where the atria meet the ventricles in the middle of the heart, that boundary is the key clue in the name atrio-ventricular.
Remember the AVN sits in the septum between the atria, just above the ventricles, so it can pass the signal down to the bundle of His.
walkthrough:
**Recall what AVN does**

Think of the name first. Atrio-ventricular means between the atria (top) and the ventricles (bottom). Its job is to pick up the wave of excitation from the atria and delay it slightly before sending it to the ventricles.

**Locate it on the diagram**

Find the central septum where the right and left sides meet, right at the base of the atria. Label B is sitting exactly there, in the top of the septum between the atria and the ventricles.

**Check the other labels**

Labels A and C are on the left and right atrioventricular valves (the tricuspid and bicuspid valves). Label D is right at the apex at the bottom of the ventricles. Only B fits the AVN position.

options.A: This is the right atrioventricular valve (tricuspid valve), not a node of conducting tissue.
options.B: This is the correct position in the septum between the atria, just above the ventricles, where the AVN delays and relays excitation to the bundle of His.
options.C: This is the left atrioventricular valve (bicuspid or mitral valve), not the AVN.
options.D: This is the apex at the bottom of the ventricles where Purkyne tissue spreads excitation, far below the AVN.
